data.title: Implement payload ingest endpoint with fCnt dedupe and base64 decode

data.to:
Implement the DRF POST endpoint from PROMPT.md that ingests an IoT payload, decodes it, dedupes it, and updates the device status. Builds on the Device/Payload models from HDT-5 and the token auth from HDT-6.

Required behavior (from PROMPT.md):
- POST to a DRF endpoint with the payload body. Example: {"fCnt": 100, "devEUI": "abcdabcdabcdabcd", "data": "AQ==", "rxInfo": [{"gatewayID": "1234123412341234", "name": "G1", "time": "2022-07-19T11:00:00", "rssi": -57, "loRaSNR": 10}], "txInfo": {"frequency": 86810000, "dr": 5}}
- fCnt is used to reject duplicate messages (scoped per device — the DB already has UniqueConstraint on (device, f_cnt)).
- The 'data' key is base64 and must be translated to a hexadecimal value. Worked example: 'AQ==' -> bytes b'\x01' -> hex '01' -> integer value 1.
- If the decoded value is 1 the payload is marked passing, otherwise failing.
- Payload connects to Device via devEUI.
- Device keeps track of its latest status value (passing vs failing).

Decisions already made (do not re-derive):
- Wire format is camelCase, model fields are snake_case — map with serializer source= (HDT-5 established this).
- Unknown devEUI auto-registers the Device via get_or_create rather than 404ing. An ingest endpoint that rejects unknown devices needs a provisioning flow that is not in scope; document this in the README so it can be changed.
- Duplicate fCnt returns 409 Conflict, not a silent 200. Explicit and testable. The IntegrityError path must be handled so a concurrent double-POST cannot 500.
- Persist the payload first, then decode/update status — models carry status default 'unknown' precisely so this ordering is possible. Keep business logic out of model save().
- Store raw base64 in Payload.data verbatim and the hex string in Payload.decoded_hex, so the decode stays re-runnable.
- received_at should be populated from rxInfo[0].time when present (HDT-5 left the field nullable for exactly this).

Also in scope: URL routing (config/urls.py + a telemetry urls module), serializers, tests covering the happy path / duplicate rejection / failing value / unauthenticated 401 / malformed base64, and README documentation with a working curl example.

Out of scope: Celery async processing, gateway/rxInfo normalization into its own model, pagination or read endpoints beyond what is needed.

data.body: Implemented per plan: serializers.py (plain Serializer, source= renames, base64+32-byte validation), services.py (decode_payload, extract_received_at with assume-UTC), PayloadIngestView (atomic persist-then-decode, IntegrityError caught outside atomic -> 409), telemetry/urls.py + config include at api/payloads/, 11 APITestCase tests, README ingest+test docs. Verified: manage.py check OK, makemigrations --check no changes, 11/11 tests pass on host Postgres (POSTGRES_PORT=5433), plus live curl e2e: 201/409/failing/401 all correct (e2e rows cleaned up). Commit 212f4df. Note: commit includes a pre-existing uncommitted '<!-- AI -->' README line left by the HDT-6 session; it belongs with that section so it rode along.

REVIEW (cold, against plan + PROMPT.md): PASS with one minor inline fix.

Verified independently:
- manage.py check: no issues. makemigrations --check --dry-run: no changes (no stray migrations).
- Full suite vs Postgres (compose db, host port 5433): 11/11 OK pre-fix; 12/12 OK after fix.
- PROMPT.md requirements all met: DRF POST /api/payloads/ (405 elsewhere), token auth via HDT-6 global defaults (401 test asserts no rows written), per-device fCnt dedupe via DB constraint alone with IntegrityError caught OUTSIDE transaction.atomic() -> 409 (verified placement; no serializer pre-check query, so no race window), base64->hex (AQ== -> 01), integer value 1 -> passing else failing (AAE= multi-byte passing pinned by test), Payload->Device via devEUI get_or_create (savepoint-protected against concurrent first registration), Device.latest_status updated in same transaction via save(update_fields) so auto_now touches updated_at.
- Edge probes beyond the suite (shell): data '' -> 400 blank; whitespace/URL-safe/unpadded base64 -> 400; 33-byte decoded -> 400, 32-byte -> valid (matches decoded_hex max_length=64); devEUI 17 chars -> 400; fCnt -1 -> 400; aware '+02:00' time passes through, naive assumed UTC (tested), garbage/empty rxInfo -> received_at None.
- Tests assert the substance, not just codes: 409 leaves exactly 1 row and latest_status unchanged; latest_status flips to failing on second frame; response body keys/values checked against DB row. No business logic in model save(); data stored verbatim; README curl/decode-rule/409/tests docs present.

FINDING (fixed inline, commit 9a94e79): fCnt >= 2**63 passed validation and raised unhandled DataError -> 500 at insert (empirically confirmed against Postgres). Violates the plan's own validation-matches-column principle (applied to devEUI and data but missed fCnt's upper bound). Fixed by max_value=9223372036854775807 on the serializer field + regression test; suite rerun 12/12 OK.

Accepted known simplifications (documented in code+README, per plan): latest_status = most-recently-ingested not highest-fCnt; strict-alphabet base64 only; 409 message assumes the only reachable IntegrityError is the (device, f_cnt) constraint - true given serializer bounds.

Verdict: PASS. Meets all acceptance criteria; moving to done.
